title: A session whose parent class changes
story: At 19:40:31 a script starts a second Claude Code process inside tmux, and the client files its SessionStart, a fresh startup, under the first session's key while that session is still live. The session began in Terminal, and now one of its session.start records names a multiplexer parent.
edits: The transcript's user entry for each prompt, read by the log reader 0.7 to 4.5 s after the hook (via log, same turn_key and lengths), as a real Claude Code client records it.
A session.start at 19:40:31.2 with the session's key, start_kind startup and parent_class multiplexer, and the presence sample the agent takes at it.

CC5.basis: one device, whose scorer credits each slot to at most one project (SM 3.1)

CC6.basis: Stated, not recomputed: the live buckets are pkg/score over this device's events.jsonl, which the reveal holds in full, so the server's re-score is the same computation and every minute reproduces.

CC10.reason: no editor act in the submission

notes: No harness records this. A new process gets a new session, and a startup names a session no other process holds. A `claude --resume` in tmux would be a resume between two interactive parents, which DESIGN 7.3 allows; this record is a startup, so CC9 fails.
A multiplexer isn't one of SM 2.2 rule 4's headless parents, so every prompt keeps its origin and CC2 still counts all five.
